To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of 10% of soy flour into wheat bread resulted in a product with good sensory attributes.
The use of 10% soya bean flour in whole wheat bread produced bread with the best nutritional and sensory quality.
the addition of soybean flour to wheat flour resulted in a decrease in the nutritional quality and increase in the functional properties of the bread.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and characterization of functional breads with improved nutritional and sensory qualities using blends of wheat and soybean flours.

the use of whole wheat flour and soybean flour as ingredients in the preparation of functional breads and to determine the effects of the substitution of soybean flour into wheat flour on the nutritional and sensory qualities of the resultant bread.
the development of functional breads from whole wheat and soy flour blends.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bread produced with a blend of 10% soya bean flour and 90% whole wheat flour was the most preferred and acceptable among the breads produced.
soybean can be used as a partial replacement for wheat flour in bread making.
the bread produced with 10% substitution of wheat with soybean flour was the most acceptable in terms of its nutritional and sensory quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soybean flour could be added to whole wheat flour in bread production at 10% without any significant effect on bread quality.
the use of soy flour at a level of 10% is recommended as it produced a bread with good nutritional composition and acceptable quality.
the use of soybean flour in the production of bread can improve its nutritional quality, however, the use of soy flour above 10% in the production of wheat bread is not recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bread can be produced with soy flour and still be of good quality.
soybean flour could be incorporated up to 10% in wheat flour for the production of functional and nutritious breads.
the addition of 10% of soybean flour to the whole wheat flour can be used to produce functional breads with good nutritional and sensory quality.
